newsitem.title: KUWAIT: OAPEC sees world demand rising 1.4 mbpd/yr to 2000.
newsitem.headline: OAPEC sees world demand rising 1.4 mbpd/yr to 2000.

text.p: The Organisation of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries (OAPEC) said it expects an annual rise of 1.4 million barrels per day (bpd) in world oil demand until the end of the century, an OAPEC report published on Monday said.

"World demand for oil is expected to continue to rise tangibly, reflecting the recovery in the rate of general world economic growth, estimated at 4.4 percent, until the end of the decade," Kuwait-based OAPEC said in its 1995 annual report.

"Estimates by (OAPEC's) general secretariat, based on the consumption trends for the past 30 years, indicate that demand could grow by seven million bpd by the end of the century. That is to say the annual rise rate would be 1.4 million bpd."
An expected turnaround in poor demand by the former Soviet republics in 1997 would be an important factor contributing to in the increase in levels of demand, it said.
But the group added that "demand would remain dependent on economic achievements and legislative measures." It did not elaborate.
OAPEC groups OPEC members Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Algeria, Iraq and Libya with non-OPEC countries Bahrain, Syria and Egypt. (Corrects to show Kuwait is an OPEC member.)
"Stagnation in demand (for OAPEC states' oil) could last for a few more years," it said.
OAPEC attributed the stagnant demand for oil from its member states to increased production from non-OPEC states and to restrictions placed by developed countries on oil consumption.
The group represents more than 60 percent of the world's proven oil reserves and a quarter of crude supplies.
